name: Environment Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public environmental data.

entries.title: European Environment Agency Datahub
entries.description: The EEA's catalogue of quality-assured environmental, climate, and sustainability data collected through its network across 38 European countries, including Copernicus services, with exploration and download.

coverage.spatial: 38 European countries (EEA member and cooperating countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (EEA legal notice; EEA materials published under CC BY)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31 in headless Chromium: HTTP 200. The Datahub says the EEA collects and quality-checks data "through our network and other institutional partners across 38 European countries" and "This datahub allows you to explore and download these data"; a featured item was the European Ground Motion Service (7 Oct 2026). The EEA legal notice (https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/legal-notice) says "EEA materials are published under the CC-BY license" and may be re-used "for commercial or non-commercial purposes, provided that the EEA is always acknowledged". The CC BY version (4.0) and the formats come from the EEA's usual practice and weren't checked here.

entries.title: EPA AirData
entries.description: EPA AirData provides access to recent and historical outdoor air quality data collected at monitoring stations across the United States, including downloadable datasets, AQI reports, and monitor information.

access.auth_note: API requires a free key obtained by email registration; bulk pre-generated files are publicly available.

entries.title: AirNow
entries.description: EPA's real-time air quality reporting program — current and forecast Air Quality Index (AQI) for ozone and particle pollution across the US, sourced from monitoring agencies.

access.auth_note: Free AirNow API key for the API.

entries.title: EPA Air Quality System (AQS)
entries.description: EPA's repository of ambient air quality data collected from state, local, and tribal monitoring agencies — criteria pollutants, hazardous air pollutants, and meteorological data.

access.auth_note: Free AQS API key (email registration); bulk pre-generated files are open.

entries.attribution: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Air Quality System

entries.title: Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO)
entries.description: EPA's portal for facility-level environmental compliance and enforcement data — inspections, violations, and enforcement actions under the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and RCRA.
entries.notes: REST services and downloadable national data sets.

entries.title: EPA EJScreen (Environmental Justice Screening and Mapping Tool)
entries.description: EPA's environmental justice screening and mapping tool and its downloadable data: environmental indicators (such as PM2.5, ozone, diesel particulate matter, traffic and hazardous-facility proximity, lead paint, Superfund proximity, wastewater discharge) combined with demographic indicators at the census block group level. EPA removed the tool and its data downloads from public access in February 2025.

recovery.notes: EPA's "Download EJScreen Data" page, captured the day before public access ended. The data files it links may or may not have been captured too; each should be checked before reuse.
EPA's technical information and data downloads page, captured the day before public access ended.
The EJScreen landing page four days before public access ended.
EPA's own January 19, 2021 website snapshot, which documents an earlier version than the 2.3 removed in 2025.

Public Environmental Data Partners' reconstruction of EJScreen version 2.3 (also served at https://pedp-ejscreen.azurewebsites.net/). It is a rebuilt copy, not EPA's, and its makers say some functions are incomplete. Nothing here verifies it against EPA's data.
A mirror of the reconstructed tool hosted by Yale's Energy History project. It is not verified against EPA's data.

coverage.spatial: United States (census block group, with state, county, city and national views)
coverage.temporal: tool public from 2015 until removal; version 2.3 (July 2024) was the last

entries.notes:
Cataloged 2026-10-31 as dark, from the open request in issue #3. On 2026-10-31, https://www.epa.gov/ejscreen returned HTTP 404 ("Page Not Found | US EPA"). The mapper host, ejscreen.epa.gov, did not answer at all (the proxy's CONNECT failed with 502). EPA's environmental justice page (https://www.epa.gov/environmentaljustice) also returned 404.
Removal date: Wikipedia's EJScreen article says "As of February 5, 2025, the EJScreen has been removed from public access" and that data "could also no longer be downloaded by users". It cites EDGI's report "EPA Removes EJScreen from Its Website" (2025-02-12, https://envirodatagov.org/epa-removes-ejscreen-from-its-website/), which returned 403 here and was not read directly. status_since uses that date. This catalog's own first observation is 2026-10-31.
Recovery candidates are ranked by authenticity, never by who runs them. The three Wayback captures and EPA's 2021 snapshot are dated copies made before the loss (timestamped); none is hash-verified, because this catalog never had a live baseline. The two community copies are reconstructions and are asserted only.
The licence is US Government work for EPA's own data. Formats (file geodatabase, CSV) and the 2015 public launch come from the tool's usual description and were not checked against the archived pages.

entries.title: EPA Envirofacts
entries.description: Integrated access to multiple EPA program databases — air, water, waste, toxics, and facility data — through a single set of REST APIs.
entries.notes: REST APIs across EPA program systems.

entries.title: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP)
entries.description: Facility-level greenhouse gas emissions data reported annually to EPA by large emitters, fuel and industrial gas suppliers, and CO2 injection sites, searchable through the FLIGHT tool and downloadable.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

entries.attribution: U.S. EPA, Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page reports "2023 Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program data is now available". It also notes a September 12, 2025 EPA proposal "to permanently remove program obligations for 46 source categories of the GHGRP". That proposal is a real risk to future coverage, so this entry is worth fingerprinting while the data is live, and a steward should watch for the rule's outcome. The 2010 start, the FLIGHT tool, and API access through Envirofacts come from the program's usual description and weren't checked here.

entries.title: EPA Superfund Sites (National Priorities List)
entries.description: EPA's searchable information on Superfund hazardous waste sites — sites proposed to, on, or deleted from the National Priorities List, sites addressed under the Superfund Alternative Approach, and non-NPL sites — by state and map.
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page offers searches for "sites proposed to, currently on, and deleted from Superfund's National Priorities List (NPL) as well as sites being addressed under the Superfund Alternative Approach (SAA)", by state (including territories such as American Samoa and Guam), with a map and advanced search for NPL and non-NPL sites. The underlying system name (SEMS), the 1980s start, and the csv export weren't checked. Environment-almanac's epa-envirofacts entry is EPA's cross-program gateway; this entry is the Superfund-specific source.

entries.title: Toxics Release Inventory (TRI)
entries.description: EPA's annual accounting of toxic chemical releases and waste management from industrial and federal facilities — the foundational US right-to-know dataset on industrial pollution.
entries.attribution: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Toxics Release Inventory
entries.notes: Bulk files and the Envirofacts API expose the full TRI.

entries.title: Eurostat Environment Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU environmental statistics and accounts — greenhouse gas and air emissions, waste, water, material flows, environmental taxes and protection expenditure, and environmental footprints.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200, page "ENVIRONMENT Database" with selected and detailed datasets. It lists "Environmental footprints based on FIGARO (2025 edition, last update: 05 November 2025)" and greenhouse gas, CO2, and methane emissions series. Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) licenses its content under CC BY 4.0. The topic list in the description reflects Eurostat's usual environment tables and wasn't checked dataset by dataset.

entries.title: OpenAQ Air Quality Data Platform
entries.description: A nonprofit platform that gathers ground-level air-quality measurements (PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, SO2, CO, black carbon) from government monitoring networks and other providers worldwide, and serves them through one API and an open archive on AWS, with each measurement traced to its source.

access.auth_note: Free API key (X-API-Key header) required for the v3 API; the AWS archive bucket was not tested for anonymous access.
access.rate_limit: 60/minute and 2,000/hour per API key (free general use); higher limits by custom agreement

coverage.spatial: global (stations in many countries; coverage depends on providers)
coverage.temporal: varies by station (example AirNow station since 2016; platform start year not checked)

entries.license: varies by source provider (per-source licences listed in the API); OpenAQ attribution required (OpenAQ Terms of Use)
entries.attribution: OpenAQ, plus the original data provider of each measurement as the API and website give it
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The home page says "OpenAQ is a nonprofit organization providing universal access to air quality data" and shows a live station card ("58 McMillan Reservoir Washington DC, US ... Provider: US EPA AirNow Reporting: Updated 3 hours ago Since 26/04/2016"). The API (https://api.openaq.org/v3/locations) answered 401 without a key, as documented: "Include your API key in the X-API-Key header of each request." The rate-limits page gives "Free ... 60 / minute 2,000 / hour". The AWS archive docs give the bucket https://openaq-data-archive.s3.amazonaws.com/ with files under /records/csv.gz/locationid=.../year=.../month=.... OpenAQ is an aggregator: it republishes measurements whose authoritative publishers are the government agencies and other providers it ingests (for the US, epa-airnow is the source entry). Cadence daily is a floor: many stations update hourly.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: OpenAQ Terms of Use (https://docs.openaq.org/about/terms) say "We only aggregate data that, to the best of our knowledge, has been made available for redistribution and use throughout the world. However, we provide no assurance that the data provided may be used free of any third-party claims", "OpenAQ users must therefore review and comply with any terms published by data providers", and "Attribution to OpenAQ as the source data is also required when using OpenAQ services for accessing the data." They also bar using the hosted API "to develop products or services that substantially duplicate or directly compete with OpenAQ's core offerings". There is no single data licence; the API's Licenses resource (https://docs.openaq.org/resources/licenses) lists each source's licence. Not checked: the licences of individual providers.

entries.title: USGS National Water Information System (NWIS)
entries.description: USGS's national archive of water-resources data — streamflow, groundwater levels, and water quality from hundreds of thousands of monitoring sites.

entries.title: Water Quality Portal
entries.description: A cooperative service of USGS, EPA, and the National Water Quality Monitoring Council providing water-quality monitoring data from over 400 federal, state, tribal, and local agencies.
entries.publisher: USGS / EPA / National Water Quality Monitoring Council
entries.notes: Standardized WQX format; programmatic web services.

entries.title: Global Nature Watch (formerly Global Forest Watch)
entries.description: World Resources Institute's forest and land monitoring platform: annual 30 m tree cover loss, near-real-time deforestation alerts, tree cover and other land datasets with country and subnational dashboards, served through maps, a data portal and a data API. Formerly named Global Forest Watch.

access.auth_note: Browsing and dataset metadata need no account; WRI's terms say many services require registering an account, and some API queries need a free key (not tested).

coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (tree cover loss 2001 onward, with 2025 included)

entries.license: varies by dataset (WRI terms of service); flagship UMD tree cover loss is CC-BY-4.0 (GFW Data API metadata)
entries.attribution: Cite each dataset as its metadata gives, e.g. Hansen et al., 2013, "High-Resolution Global Maps of 21st-Century Forest Cover Change", accessed through Global Nature Watch on [date], www.globalnaturewatch.org
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 after a 301 redirect: the issue's URL https://www.globalforestwatch.org/ now redirects to https://globalnaturewatch.org/, which is catalogued here. The page reads "Global Forest Watch is now Global Nature Watch. A new name for the next chapter of our work — continuing to advance forest monitoring while expanding monitoring coverage and capabilities. Our name has changed, but our commitment remains the same and your workflows will continue to be supported." Old dashboard paths redirect too (/dashboards/global/), and https://data.globalforestwatch.org/ still answered 200. The GFW Data API (https://data-api.globalforestwatch.org/datasets) listed 382 datasets; umd_tree_cover_loss is at version v1.13, metadata updated 2026-08-05, "annual, 30m, global, UMD GLAD", with images used "for 2023, 2024 and 2025". The main tree cover loss data is produced by the University of Maryland GLAD lab (with Google, USGS and NASA) and served by WRI here; GLAD's own copy is at https://glad.earthengine.app/view/global-forest-change. The geotiff format, the alert products and the API key rules weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: WRI's terms (https://globalnaturewatch.org/terms/, reached from the old /terms/ URL) say "Open data is important to Us and we make considerable effort to make many of the datasets available without restriction through the Services. Nonetheless, each dataset carries its own license and restrictions. You should review the dataset's metadata to understand these restrictions." The tree cover loss metadata in the Data API gives "license": "CC BY 4.0". Other datasets' licences weren't checked.
